TL;DR

A stylish, Left 4 Dead–inspired co-op shooter with great vibes and some smart ideas, but not enough content or momentum to keep players long-term.

Full Review

Quick clarification up front — because I’m consistent about this:
I usually only review games I have beaten.
The Anacrusis doesn’t really work that way.
What it does have is enough matches played to understand what it’s trying to be — and why it struggled to stick.

The Anacrusis wears its inspiration openly. This is a four-player co-op shooter clearly built in the shadow of Left 4 Dead, but wrapped in a retro-futuristic sci-fi aesthetic that immediately sets it apart visually. The art direction is clean, colorful, and memorable in a way most modern shooters aren’t.

Moment to moment, the game feels solid. Shooting works, movement is fine, and working together to survive waves of enemies scratches that familiar co-op itch. When things get hectic, the game can still deliver those classic “save your teammate at the last second” moments.

The problem is depth and longevity.

Enemy variety is limited, missions start to blend together, and progression doesn’t provide enough long-term motivation. The AI director system is there, but it doesn’t feel as dynamic or surprising as the games it’s inspired by. Once you’ve seen most of what The Anacrusis offers, there isn’t a strong pull to keep coming back.

Playing with friends helps — a lot. Like most co-op shooters, the experience lives or dies based on who you’re playing with. With a good group, it’s fun. Without one, it’s easy to bounce off.

The biggest issue is momentum. Updates came slowly, the player base dropped, and the game never quite found the footing it needed to grow. There’s a solid foundation here, but not enough support to turn it into something lasting.

The Anacrusis isn’t bad.
It just never became essential.

Steam Deck Performance

Playable on Steam Deck. Performance is generally stable, and the game runs fine in handheld mode. Controls work with the default layout, though you may see mouse/keyboard prompts at times. Like most co-op shooters, it’s more comfortable with a full controller setup, but it’s absolutely usable on Deck.

Pros

Strong retro sci-fi art direction

Familiar, approachable co-op shooter design

Fun with friends

Clean presentation

Cons

Limited content and enemy variety

Weak long-term progression

Relies heavily on having a group

Lost momentum post-launch

Verdict

A co-op shooter with great style and solid fundamentals that never fully realized its potential. The Anacrusis is enjoyable in short bursts, especially with friends, but lacks the depth and support needed to keep players invested long-term.
